units.translation: Pollux 2, 100: στόμιν [hard-mouthed] (the manuscripts have στόμα [mouth] or ἄστομον [without a mouth]) Aeschylus used for the rough (horse). Phrynichus in Bekker p. 64, 14: στόμις [hard-mouthed] (στόμης in the codex) and a violent horse: one that does not obey the bit. Photius p. 540, 16 and Suidas: στόμις [hard-mouthed] (στομίας in Suidas) horse: disobedient and violent. Hesychius: στόμις [hard-mouthed] (στομίς in the codex): the disobedient one, having a large mouth. And they call horses στόμιας [hard-mouthed] (στομίας in the codex) those that disobey the bits.
50 στόμις [hard-mouthed] in Aeschylus is the horse that, as it were, pushes back with its mouth against the bits.
